summary: A scholar in Tibetology and religious studies, Eric David Mortensen received his PhD from Harvard University (attested 2003) under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton. He also studied under Chongren He, Xiaoxun He, Zhiben He, Xi Aniu, and Xuewen He.

Eric Grinstead was a sinologist and computational linguist who studied at Victoria University of Wellington from circa 1946 to 1950. He later held posts at the British Library (circa 1957–1970) and the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies in 1969.

Specializing in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Eric Haruki Swanson has served in posts at Loyola Marymount University and at Stanford University, where he is attested as a Senior Visiting Scholar in 2026.
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe studied at Hartley Victoria College, Manchester, and Uppsala. A scholar of religious studies and Indology, he taught at Manchester, Lancaster, and Uppsala, and held the First Chair of Religious Studies at the University of Sydney (1977–1996).

Eric M. Greene, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, earned his PhD at UC Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf. He also studied under Toru Funayama, Kunio Mugitani, Kenji Kinugawa, and Nobumi Iyanaga, before holding religious studies posts at Yale University.

Eric Stephen Goodell, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completed master's degrees at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia (attested 2012), where he studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner.

Erich Frauwallner was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna. He served as professor and director at Vienna between 1928 and 1964 and founded the Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Südasiens in 1957.

Erich Haenisch studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Wilhelm Grube. A scholar of Sinology and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he held professorships at the University of Göttingen (1925), University of Leipzig (~1925–1932), Berlin (1932), and University of Munich (1927–1951).

Erich Heintel was an Austrian philosophy scholar who completed his doctorate (1931–1936) and habilitation (1940) at the University of Vienna. He served there as extraordinary professor from 1952 and as ordinary professor of philosophy from 1960 to 1982.

Erich Rudolf Jaensch studied at Breslau, Göttingen (PhD 1907), and Strasbourg (Habilitation 1911). A scholar of philosophy, he held posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1912–1913) and the University of Marburg as ordinary professor beginning in 1913.

Erik Braun is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his degree at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso, also studying with Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun. By 2026, he is attested on the faculty at the University of Virginia.

Erik Haarh was a Tibetologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Copenhagen. He worked at the Royal Danish Library (1956–1962) and served at Aarhus University as head of History/Religion (1969) and professor of theology (1983).

Erik J. Hammerstrom is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2010). He held a post as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).
Erik Pema Kunsang is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies specialist. His career includes posts as director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications and resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark.

Erik Zürcher was a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Leiden University, studying under Paul Demiéville, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, Édouard Chavannes, and J. J. L. Duyvendak. He served as Director at Leiden (1961–1993) and co-edited T'oung Pao.

Erik-Jan Zürcher studied at Leiden University (BA, PhD). Specializing in history, archaeology, and linguistics, he held posts at Radboud University Nijmegen, the International Institute of Social History, the University of Amsterdam, and Leiden University as professor of Turkish language and culture (1997).

Sinologist Erling von Mende studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, Bonn, and Cologne (PhD 1969, Habilitation 1979). He served as university professor of Sinology at the Free University of Berlin from 1983 to 2007.
Ernest Arthur Gardner was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Gonville and Caius College from circa 1880 to 1884. He later held a post at the University of London from 1924 to 1926.

Ernest Bender was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Zellig S. Harris, and Henry Hoenigswald. He served as assistant, associate, and full professor at Pennsylvania between 1950 and 1989.
